answer.origin: Joint NVIDIA and OpenAI announcement dated 2026-08-17, as reported by the New York Post the same day; cross-checked against NVIDIA's own 2026-08-17 blog post and Form 8-K exhibit filing (EDGAR).
answer.note: The 2026-08-17 headline says NVIDIA will provide up to $105 billion in financing toward OpenAI's Ohio data center. NVIDIA's own 8-K filing describes the substance more narrowly. On 2026-08-17 NVIDIA entered into multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy, the lessor, covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site in Ohio. NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation under the initial guaranty commitment is capped at $105 billion. The guaranty pays a lease-value shortfall if OpenAI, the tenant, becomes insolvent and defaults or fails to pay lease rent. OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for amounts actually paid. The guaranty generally becomes effective when each lease commences, and payments are conditional on the lessor meeting ready-for-service conditions expected from 2028. NVIDIA says its support is limited to defined portions of lease and power payments plus a specified residual-value commitment, not the full site cost or all tenant obligations. My reading is that the $105 billion is a contingent guaranty cap, not a cash financing outlay already made. It is still a signed, binding NVIDIA obligation tied to OpenAI's lease, which is the substance the earlier reported talks about a backstop were about. The reported $250 billion, $350 billion and $500 billion-plus figures from July and August are not confirmed by this filing and should not be read as this agreement's size.
limitations: The $105 billion is a cap on NVIDIA's initial guaranty payment obligation under the agreements, not a disclosed amount of cash financing provided or drawn.
The filing excerpt does not disclose the lease term, rent amounts, or the total lease-value guaranteed, so the size of the guaranteed exposure relative to the $105 billion cap is unknown.
Payment is conditional on lease commencement and the lessor's ready-for-service conditions, expected to begin in 2028; whether those conditions will be met is not known.
No debt financing for the Ohio project is disclosed in the reviewed records. Whether any lender-facing debt facility exists, and whether NVIDIA guarantees it, is not established.
The reported separate $350 billion chip-purchase financing discussions are not addressed by this filing and remain unconfirmed.
The NVIDIA blog and 8-K are NVIDIA-originated documents, so their agreement with the joint announcement does not count as independent corroboration of the terms.
follow_up: Read the full text of NVIDIA's 2026-08-17 Form 8-K and its exhibits to confirm the guaranty structure, the $105 billion cap, the effectiveness conditions and whether any debt financing is guaranteed.
Check later NVIDIA or SB Energy filings and press for lease commencement dates, ready-for-service milestones and any amendment or termination of the Portsmouth guaranty agreements.
Check whether OpenAI or SB Energy disclose the lease term, rent and financing structure for the Portsmouth Site to size the guaranteed exposure.
Check whether any separate NVIDIA backstop for lender debt is signed, since the question also allows debt financing as the guaranteed item.

updates.statement: Rung 1 (Yes) is now better supported than rung 2. On 2026-08-17, before the 2026-12-31 deadline, NVIDIA's 8-K reports that it entered into multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy, the lessor, covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site, with an initial guaranty payment obligation capped at $105 billion. OpenAI is the tenant, and NVIDIA covers a lease-value shortfall if OpenAI becomes insolvent and defaults or fails to pay lease rent, with OpenAI agreeing to reimburse NVIDIA. This is a signed, binding NVIDIA guarantee of OpenAI's data-center lease obligations, which matches the question's lease-guarantee branch. The earlier rung 2 lean assumed the proposed backstop was still unsigned and non-binding, which the filing now contradicts. Residual uncertainty is about classification: the instrument is a residual value guaranty of lease payments, not a loan guarantee, and payments are contingent on lease commencement and ready-for-service conditions expected from 2028.
limitations: The guaranty is contingent: NVIDIA pays only on a defined trigger such as OpenAI's default, and payments depend on lessor ready-for-service conditions expected from 2028.
The $105 billion is a cap, not a cash amount provided. The filing does not show a debt financing guarantee, so the debt branch of the question is unestablished.
Whether a residual value guaranty on lease payments counts as guaranteeing financing for the lease is a classification judgement, not stated in the filing.
what_would_change_it: A resolver or the question wording that excludes residual value guaranties on lease payments from 'guarantee financing for the data-center lease'.
Amendment or termination of the 2026-08-17 guaranty agreements before 2026-12-31.
Evidence that the guaranty agreements were not binding at signing, for example conditions precedent that make them non-binding until a later event.
